title.narrative: Women Advocate for Peace (Women, Peace and Security in Colombia)

description.narrative: Our Theory of Change describes three mutually interrelated thematic pillars/ result areas: 1. Peace process; 2. Accompaniment and protection; and 3. Women’s empowerment. The fulfilment of the gender indicators established by the Peace Accord will influence the application and adoption of gender-based measures to protect women, including psychosocial attention. Compliance with the gender measures established by the Peace Accord is a determining factor for a sustainable and inclusive peace process. By accompanying women and their organizations, they will become stronger, increase their resilience, and be able to participate in political spaces to ensure the application and monitoring of the current laws governing gender (including the WPS agenda and SDG-5) at the national as well as departmental and municipal levels. Finally, encouraging their economic autonomy and a more equitable redistribution of chores in the family context will facilitate their empowerment, the development of their political role, and their fundamental contribution to development and peace in Colombia.

“Women Advocate for Peace” aims to contribute to a lasting peace process with gender justice in Colombia, in which women and girls have equal rights and opportunities as men and boys. This implies creating enabling conditions to strengthen the participation, influence and leadership of women and their organisations in peace-building spaces at the local, territorial and national levels. This five-year programme from 2021 to 2025 has been elaborated by a consortium consisting of three Colombian organizations—Ruta Pacífica de la Mujeres, Liga Internacional de Mujeres por la Paz y la Libertad (LIMPAL) and Corporación de Apoyo a Comunidades Populares (CODACOP)—and two Dutch ones—ICCO and HealthNet TPO.

title.narrative: Strengthened capacity of women, women's rights organizations, CSOs to enhance women's rights, empowerment and gender equality

comment.narrative: The participating women belonging to the Kamentsa Biya indigenous group in Putumayo did not carry out organisational processes that would allow them to strengthen their psychosocial and psychocultural capacities to promote their autonomy, as well as strategies for active community participation. In alliance with the Jajañ Corporation, a process of capacity building for advocacy and prevention of GBV has been initiated, as well as the exchange of health and advocacy practices with the indigenous women of the Nasa community of the organisation "Tejido Mujer".

In 2024, HNTPO continued working with and training the Kämentsá community, who have since begun training other women within their own communities. Additionally, it was launched a new training process with a group of 14 older women from La Macarena, Meta.This process spanned 18 sessions held between 2023 and 2024, focusing on capacity building in gender-based violence (GBV) prevention, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) tools, self-care and collective care practices, and advocacy skills. The women named their group “Mujeres que lideran con valentía”—“Women Who Lead with Courage.”They were equipped with printed resources including the Guía Emma, Psychological First Aid materials, information on UN Resolution 1325, Law 1257, and relevant infographics. The group also initiated community mobilization activities to raise awareness about GBV, collaborated with HNTPO on school-based efforts to prevent GBV and promote collective care among young women, and began replicating parts of their training with other groups

In 2025, the two existing groups continued their training processes. The group of Indigenous Kämentsá women remained active in replicating the training sessions within their own communities. Meanwhile, the group from La Macarena, Meta, also began replicating their training and expressed a desire for further sessions, specifically focused on collective care strategies.This year, we also launched a new training initiative in collaboration with La Mesa de Víctimas (The Effective Participation Board of Victims) in La Macarena, Meta. This institutional platform allows victims of the armed conflict to actively participate in the discussion, evaluation, training, and oversight of public policies related to their assistance and reparation. As a key element of the National System for Comprehensive Assistance and Reparation to Victims (SNARIV), the Board plays a vital role in ensuring victims have a meaningful voice in decision-making processes that impact them.As part of this initiative, we conducted an initial awareness session on gender-based violence (GBV) with the full board. We then began a dedicated training process with the women members of the board, carrying out three 5-hour sessions. These sessions focused on:Identifying, distinguishing, and preventing different forms of GBV; Raising awareness of available support mechanisms for GBV cases; Strengthening psychological first aid skillsDeepening understanding of Resolution 1325 and Law 1257, emphasizing their importance in protecting women and girls, promoting rights, and contextualizing GBV within the framework of the armed conflictSummary of 2025 Activities:We are currently working with three active groups:Kämentsá Women Who Advocate for Peace – Sibundoy, PutumayoWomen Who Lead with Courage – La Macarena, MetaWomen from the Effective Participation Board of Victims – La Macarena, MetaIn total, 56 women are participating in the training: 49 older women and 7 young women.

For 2023, two strategies will be consolidated for women's advocacy in their communities and local government: 1) an audiovisual strategy on the importance of ancestral medicine practices for the prevention of GBV will be consolidated and 2)local spaces for discussion will be created around the intersection between the right to health and the right to territorial and food sovereignty.

Pedagogical meetings are being held to strengthen capacities in the areas of: Self-care and wellbeing, agriculture and wellbeing, ancestral medicine and mental health, political advocacy and sovereignty and referral pathways for GBV. HNTPO is promoting political advocacy actions to strengthen the participation and skills of indigenous Kämentsá Biyá women in the decision-making scenarios of their own government. In the second quarter of 2023, HNTPO's actions in the municipality of Sibundoy, Department of Putumayo, have involved 124 women over 28 years of age. Among these, 20 women over 28 years of age are participating in the specific process of training and strengthening of skills in mental health and psychosocial support. As a result, the participation and leadership of women who had not previously participated in decision-making spaces has been promoted, as well as work on decision-making and conflict resolution strategies for the group's own dynamics and their place as women in the prevention of GBV. The process of strengthening capacities and knowledge for GBV prevention will be measured based on the pre-test and post-test that WAP Colombia has in its process of measuring the GBV component. The post-test will be applied in September at the end of the capacity building sessions. An interdepartmental alliance was established in the third quarter between HNTPO and the University of Nariño, Colombia. This alliance aims to further strengthening the capacity and knowledge sharing of the indigenous women from the Kämentsá Biyá community. This process had a particular focus on political advocacy and the deconstruction of stereotypes and cultural practices that support the prevalence of cases of GBV. This was developed within the framework of the political structure of the indigenous government.

Through the intergenerational meeting with young women, we especially seek to promote their participation in community radio, through which a mini-series of themes for the prevention of GBV in indigenous communities will be made. The process of strengthening capacities and knowledge for GBV prevention will be measured based on the pre-test and post-test that WAP Colombia has in its process of measuring the GBV component. The post-test will be applied in September at the end of the capacity building sessions. In the second quarter of 2023, HNTPO's actions in the municipality of Sibundoy, Department of Putumayo, have involved 58 women under 28 years of age. HNTPO is promoting political advocacy actions to strengthen the participation and skills of indigenous Kämentsá Biyá women in the decision-making scenarios of their own government. Among these, 8 women under 20 years of age are participating in the specific process of training and strengthening of skills in mental health and psychosocial support. As a result, the participation and leadership of women who had not previously participated in decision-making spaces has been promoted, as well as work on decision-making and conflict resolution strategies for the group's own dynamics and their place as women in the prevention of GBV. HNTPO established in the third quarter an interdepartmental alliance with the University of Nariño, Colombia, in order to certify the capacity strengthening process that HealthNet TPO has been developing with the group of indigenous women from the Kämentsá Biyá community. This certification process has focused on strengthening capacities and knowledge sharing for the prevention of GBV and promoting young women participation via schools and local radio.
